text:
Predicates:
Engaged(x) ::: x is engaged.
MakeWeddingPlans(x) ::: x makes wedding plans.
Invite(x, y) ::: x invites y to their ceremony.
WellAttendedWedding(x) ::: x has a well-attended wedding.
LargerFamily(x) ::: x has a larger family.
John ::: John is the individual in question.

Premises:
∀x (MakeWeddingPlans(x) → Engaged(x)) ::: All people who make wedding plans are engaged.
∀x (Invite(x, y) → MakeWeddingPlans(x)) ::: All who invite others make wedding plans.
∀x (WellAttendedWedding(x) → ∃y Invite(x, y)) ::: Anyone with a well-attended wedding invites others.
∃x (LargerFamily(x) ∧ WellAttendedWedding(x)) ∨ ∃x (LargerFamily(x) ∧ Invite(x, y)) ::: Some with larger families have well-attended weddings or invite others.
Engaged(John) → (¬Invite(John, y) ∧ MakeWeddingPlans(John)) ::: If John is engaged, then John does not invite friends and makes wedding plans.
LargerFamily(John) → (WellAttendedWedding(John) ∨ ∃y Invite(John, y)) ::: If John has a larger family, then John has a well-attended wedding or invites friends.
